editorial:
Imagine getting a front-row seat to the final days of one of the biggest scammers in history. You get to follow Elizabeth Holmes right before she goes to jail, but there is a catch. Nathan Fielder is running the cameras, and he is known for making people look silly or awkward. At first, it feels like a normal interview, but the vibe quickly shifts. You start to wonder who is actually in control here. It is a wild ride that feels less like a news report and more like a strange social experiment that just keeps going.

What really works is how the movie tricks you. Just when you think you have figured out the point, the story takes a hard turn that leaves you questioning everything you just saw. The pacing is great, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you want a fast action movie. If you like true crime or just love seeing rich people get called out, you need to see this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch every weird look on her face, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you like owning your movies.
endingExplained: The big twist happens when you realize the whole three-year project was a setup by Nathan Fielder. He didn't just film her; he manipulated her surroundings to see if she would lie again. In the final scene, Elizabeth realizes she has been played the entire time. The movie ends with her staring into the camera in total silence, finally looking like a normal person instead of a fake CEO.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and true crime stories.
